A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LDR research work. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-F support comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v2 reports original GMM and molecular sampling experiments in Sections 4.2-4.5, with additional ablations, numerical results and visualizations in Appendices D-F.

after.justification: v3 retains the original GMM and molecular sampling results, including unbiased, biased, variational and Cartesian-coordinate experiments and their appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The LDR objectives, off-policy procedure, flow architectures, annealing algorithm and Cartesian augmentation correction are retained. The optimizer revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same GMM, alanine dipeptide and alanine hexapeptide under the same training scenarios and coordinate representations. The GMM test-set specification concerns sample counts within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Forward KL, path-gradient forward KL, FAB, TA-BG and CMT remain in their corresponding comparisons. The sampling-speed comparator in Table 5 and the appendix comparator sets are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendices B.5-B.6 revise settings within retained experiments. GMM NLL uses 10,000 test samples and ESS uses 100,000 model samples, replacing v2's general 10-million-sample statement; GMM batches are 50/100/1,000 instead of the blanket 1,024. Cartesian training specifies AdamW instead of the blanket Adam setting. Cartesian evaluation discards samples with the top 0.2% of weights for ESS and clips the top 0.2% for reweighted Ramachandran metrics, replacing the general 0.01% clipping description. These reported protocol revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the loss-weight sensitivity, LDR-only failure demonstration, additional penalty variants, gradient-variance analysis and reduced-budget CMT experiments. The path-gradient analyses and Figure 9 visualizations also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Result tables retain four independent runs, except three for variational hexapeptide, with standard deviations and uncorrected two-sided Welch's t-tests at alpha=0.05. The qualification that these capture seed-level variability is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, rankings and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains Cartesian LDR-L2 ESS of 35.89 ± 1.69%. No results are added or removed despite the revised setting descriptions.

T1.justification: Propositions A.1-A.3, the gradient derivations in A.4, the annealing mathematics and the augmentation proof and correction in C.1 are unchanged. Mathematical passages only reflow.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about off-policy LDR, improved performance and data efficiency, and savings of up to an order of magnitude.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning heavy-tailed weights, L1/L2 stability, normalization and path gradients are retained. Limitations concerning loss-weight tuning, biased references and transferability are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B.4-B.6 add reproducibility details, including the separate GMM test set, general Adam weight decay of 1e-5 with no GMM weight decay, and TarFlow's AdamW betas (0.9, 0.95), weight decay 4e-4 and gradient-norm clipping at 1.0. Hardware, training times and code/data access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged. Bibliographic revisions expand journal names, such as Nature Machine Intelligence, while retaining the same publications.

P1.justification: Short additions and qualifications in B.4-B.6 distinguish GMM, internal-coordinate and Cartesian settings. Journal names and the version/date stamp are updated; the main narrative and section order are retained.

P2.justification: Appendix reflow relocates existing displays: Table 8 moves from page 22 to 23, Table 9 from 26 to 27, Figure 5 from 25 to 26, and Figure 8 from 27 to 28. Their contents, captions and display structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices B.4-B.6 replace overgeneralized settings with experiment-specific evaluation counts, weight handling and optimizer details, making the existing results easier to reproduce and assess. The scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged, and reruns are not established, so the improvement is limited to technical reporting and transparency.
